definition: Algedonic aesthetics is a historical term for viewing aesthetics as a branch of the study of pleasure and pain, especially hedonics. In this sense, aesthetic experience is considered in relation to feelings of pleasure and suffering.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Algedonic Aesthetics; pinned source text

reasons: “Suffering” is not supported by the source packet, which refers to pleasure and pain, not suffering.

The wording shifts from the packet’s historical definition of aesthetics as a branch of hedonics / the science of pleasure and pain to a broader claim about aesthetic experience that is not explicitly stated in the source.

The definition’s phrase “aesthetic experience is considered in relation to feelings of pleasure and suffering” is not stated in the packet; the packet instead says “Aesthetics considered as a special branch…” and does not explicitly mention “aesthetic experience” or “feelings.”
While the packet supports “pleasure and pain” and “especially hedonics,” it does not support the specific framing of “pleasure and suffering” as “feelings” tied to aesthetic experience.
